label: first copy step (output orig(1), input = first token) in very short sequences starting with a/m/p/k/b/u
explanation: Sparse feature (~0.02% of steps). 89% of activation mass is at the step right after <DEL>, where the model has fed back its first output orig(0) and is now emitting orig(1) (recall_idx==1). It is almost entirely restricted to short sequences: L=3 holds 64% of mass and L=4 holds 26%. It is further keyed to the first token: a (11x lift) > m, p > k, b > u. The top activations are L=3 sequences that start with a, have u as the second token and o or 2 as the last (e.g. a u o <DEL> [a] u). Second token u and last token o/2/c raise magnitude, but conditioning on these did not improve the predicate. It does not fire in the original phase (11% of mass, scattered at t=3-5 near the end of length-4/5 inputs), at the delimiter step, or at later copy steps. It is nearly silent for L>=5. Precision stays low (about 1/3) because many L=3 sequences that start with these tokens do not activate. The firing depends on a conjunction of token identities that a simple predicate cannot capture.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: L=4 & t=5 (+5.62), orig0=a (+4.92), prev_tok=2 (+4.09), orig0=b (+3.73), orig0=p (+3.57), orig0=k (+3.47). Lower it: orig1=y (-2.03), prev3_tok=- (-2.02), orig_idx=-1 (-1.73).
